summary: Intermittent APAC-egress routing observed for EU-pinned dedicated tenant causing p95 latency jitter
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (DataMill Analytics, dedicated tenant) reports intermittent high p95 latency for inference calls from EU-based traffic. Tenant is pinned to eu-west pool but we are seeing a subset of requests routed via ap-southeast-1 which increases p95 from ~180ms to ~850ms.

Impact:
- Production traffic for DataMill analytics pipelines experiencing periodic p95 spikes (~0.5%–2% of requests during rolling windows).
- Errors are not increased; primary impact is latency and customer SLA concern.

Environment:
- Tenant: datamill-prod (dedicated gpu pool)
- Region: eu-west primary pin configured via tenant routing policy (strict_pin: false by default)
- Time window: first observed 2026-03-09 18:20 UTC, reproducible intermittently through 2026-03-10

Steps to reproduce:
1. Send batched generation requests for model redwood-1-large pinned to tenant datamill-prod from EU IPs.
2. Observe latency distribution in Console -> Per-route latency (p50/p95/p99).
3. Correlate request IDs that show p95 > 500ms with router decision logs.

Observed logs / snippets:
- Example request IDs (observed high p95): rqd_20260309_7a1b, rqd_20260310_10c3
- Router decision trace (extracted): route.decide(tenant=datamill-prod, geo=eu) -> selected_edge=eu-west-3 primary, fallback_path=[ap-southeast-1] -> chosen=edge=ap-southeast-1 due to available_capacity_low=true at timestamp 2026-03-10T09:12:18Z
- Network traceroute excerpt from selected host: 10 hops, transit via sfo -> ap-southeast-1 (unexpected)

Initial hypothesis:
1) Autoscaler or capacity scoring occasionally marks eu-west pool as low-capacity causing smart-router to choose apac pool as low-cost fallback, even when tenant pinned.
2) Sticky pin TTL or route-staleness in our control-plane allows short-lived multipath routing for dedicated tenants when strict_pin is not set.
3) Mis-evaluation of latency/cost scoring metric in smart-routing that underweights geo-penalty in edge cases.

Investigation notes:
- Confirmed: tenant routing policy shows pin to eu-west but strict_pin=false; that means fallback to compatible variants is allowed by policy.
- Checked autoscaler metrics for eu-west pool around timestamps: GPU utilization spiked to 92% for 30s windows; however capacity autoscaler added nodes but with a 45s startup delay. During that window routing score favoured ap-southeast-1.
- Router trace logs show a weight calculation: score = latency_est + cost_adj - pin_bonus; pin_bonus incorrectly set to 5 for dedicated tenants in recent config rollout (should be 20).
- Found related deployment PR that adjusted pin bonus to be dynamic: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/3412 (author: infra/team). The change was merged 2026-03-08 and rolled out 2026-03-09.

Customer-provided context:
- They enforce EU data processing but rely on our documented routing policy that pin=tenant should keep traffic in-region except for strict_pin override. They do not have strict_pin enabled because they depended on cost-aware fallback being region-aware.

Temporary mitigation applied (2026-03-10 14:45 UTC):
- Flipped per-tenant override: set strict_pin=true for datamill-prod via control plane to force hard residency until fix. Notified customer of short maintenance (no downtime).
- Added routing metric alert for when >0.1% of tenant requests are routed outside pinned region.

Next steps (planned):
- Roll back the recent pin_bonus change in routing config (PR drafted) to restore stronger pin weighting for dedicated tenants. Owner: infra-routing team.
- Add a unit/regression test to assert pin_bonus minimum for dedicated and private tenants.
- Improve autoscaler warm-up smoothing to avoid transient low_capacity signals.
- Follow up with customer on SLA credits and permanent config options (allowing them to opt into strict_pin or dedicated hard-residency).

Resolution (partial):
- Temporary: strict_pin=true for tenant (workaround) which reduced outside-region routing to <0.01% during observation window.
- Permanent: PR to revert/adjust routing pin bonus pending review.
comments: 2026-03-10 12:05 UTC - Avery Chen (support): Customer reported p95 jump to ~850ms for a subset of requests. Created ticket and opened investigation. Included initial traces and request IDs.

2026-03-10 12:30 UTC - Jordan Patel (SRE): Pulled router decision logs and autoscaler metrics. Noted eu-west pool transient utilization spike and fallback to ap-southeast-1. Escalating to infra-routing.
2026-03-10 13:10 UTC - Priya Nair (infra-routing): Confirmed recent config change reduced pin_bonus in scoring. Recommending immediate per-tenant strict_pin toggle as stopgap.
2026-03-10 14:50 UTC - Avery Chen (support): Applied strict_pin=true for datamill-prod at customer's request. Monitoring shows p95 normalized. Customer informed; awaiting infra PR.
2026-03-11 09:20 UTC - Priya Nair (infra-routing): Opened PR to adjust pin bonus minimum and added regression tests. Link: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/3450. Assigned reviewers.

2026-03-12 08:40 UTC - Customer (DataMill Ops - Carlos Mendez): Confirmed that after strict_pin change p95 decreased and notebooks resumed. Asked for permanent config option and rationale note for audit. Asked about billing/SLA credits for impacted window.
investigation_notes: Key finding: routing scoring change merged 2026-03-09 reduced pin influence for dedicated tenants. Combined with autoscaler warm-up delay, some requests were routed to APAC fallback, increasing p95. Verified by matching router decision logs and autoscaler metrics and the merge PR. Temporary strict_pin set for tenant reduced out-of-region routing. Next: revert pin change and harden tests.
resolution: Workaround: strict_pin=true applied for datamill-prod which eliminated the observed p95 spikes. Permanent fix: infra-routing to revert/adjust routing pin_bonus and add regression tests; autoscaler warm-up smoothing work item created. Customer to receive postmortem and SLA credit evaluation.
